title: Ketogenic diet mediates intestinal tumorigenesis through lipids not ketones.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: GEO series GSE334093 (mouse small-intestine scRNA-seq, single-cell RNA sequencing): listed the 4 supplementary files and their sizes (matrix .mtx.gz 104 MB, barcodes 66 KB, features 103 KB, metadata 108 KB). Downloaded the metadata and barcodes: 15,053 cells from 4 mice (Cont_KTD1 3,549, Cont_KTD2 4,896, KTD1 3,194, KTD2 3,414), all male; columns include diet_condition (ControlDiet 8,445 / KetoDiet 6,608) and cell_type_anno (7 epithelial types). Barcode count matches metadata. Did not download the 104 MB count matrix (over the 50 MB cap).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (paywalled, no PMCID, no full text or supplement in Europe PMC). Tumour burden, survival and genetic-knockout phenotype data are not in any open repository I found; they would be in Nature source-data files I could not access.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO files download openly (checked metadata and barcodes); count matrix is 104 MB, above the 50 MB cap, so only its size was recorded.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: diet_condition and cell_type_anno are columns in the metadata file (seen in the file). The paper's main outcome, tumour burden, is not in the deposited data at all.

a3_inputs_present.note: Gene-by-cell count matrix with a features file is present (seen in listing, not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: Raw UMI (unique molecular identifier) counts in Matrix Market format; standard for 10x data.

a5_enough_rows.note: 15,053 cells, but the independent unit for the diet label is the mouse: 4 mice, 2 per diet (seen in biosample_id). Diet is perfectly confounded with sample, so any cell-level classifier learns mouse/batch identity.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~104 MB compressed sparse matrix, ~1-2 GB in memory

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO lists 4 samples and the metadata has 4 biosamples; barcodes (15,053) match metadata rows. Paper text not available to cross-check cell numbers.

a8_label_provenance.note: cell_type_anno is the authors' clustering-based annotation computed from the same expression features, so predicting it is circular. diet_condition is a real experimental label but is identical to mouse ID (see A5).

backbone.name: scGPT / Geneformer (single-cell foundation models) would match the data type

honest_claim_h3: A model could only claim to separate cells from these 2 ketogenic-diet mice from cells of these 2 control mice, which cannot be distinguished from mouse or batch effects.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression of mouse gut lining cells to predict whether the mouse ate a ketogenic or control diet.
plain_idea.train_on: Gene expression counts for 15,053 intestinal epithelial cells (verified), drawn from only 4 mice.
plain_idea.predict: Diet group (ketogenic vs control), known from the experimental design; or cell type, which the authors assigned by clustering the same expression data.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little: with 2 mice per diet, any signal is inseparable from mouse-to-mouse and batch differences, and the paper's real outcome (tumour burden) is not deposited.

label_elsewhere.sources: Not assessed in depth (rejected at Part A).

ml_idea: Diet-state classification from intestinal scRNA-seq; not viable because the label has only 4 independent mice and cell-type labels are derived from the expression features.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes only; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count independent mice per diet in biosample_id: 2 vs 2, which kills it (done).

verdict_reason: Deposited data is one small scRNA-seq experiment of 4 mice (2 per diet), so the diet label has n=4 and is confounded with sample; cell-type labels come from clustering the same features; tumour outcome data are not openly deposited.
